prompt: Complete Ranges: inRange(lo, hi) returns an IntPredicate that tests inclusive membership, and countWhere counts the elements of an int[] that satisfy a predicate.
explanation: IntPredicate is the primitive specialization of Predicate for int, avoiding boxing: its test method takes a bare int. inRange is a factory method that captures lo and hi in a lambda, producing a reusable, composable test -- and because negate() and and() are default methods on the interface, any lambda you return automatically supports them. countWhere then shows the other side of the contract: code that consumes a predicate without caring how it was built.
hints: inRange should return a lambda taking one int: v -> (some boolean expression using lo, hi and v).
Inclusive on both ends means lo <= v && v <= hi.
In countWhere, loop over the array and increment a counter whenever p.test(v) is true.
